## File: README.md

# client

**The frontend SDK for MGPL Diagnostics: typed, headless, zero dependencies.**

Your UI, your design system, your UX. The backend renders the reports and invoices; this talks to it.

[![Frontend](https://img.shields.io/badge/side-frontend-14264A)](#)
[![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-14264A)](#)
[![Size](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-%E2%89%88%205%20KB-14264A)](#)
[![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20hooks-optional-C2410C?logo=react&logoColor=white)](#react-optional)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-All%20rights%20reserved-E9A23B)](LICENSE)

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [GraphQL](#graphql-the-whole-backend) · [SDK](#the-sdk) · [React](#react-optional) · [Errors & auth](#errors-and-auth) · [Docs](docs/api.md)

</div>

---

<img src="docs/images/create-report.png" alt="A result-entry form built on the SDK, with a live preview rendered by the backend" />
<p align="center"><sub>A result-entry form generated from <code>GET /templates</code>, with a live preview from the backend (the <a href="https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-studio">report-studio</a> demo). Every pixel of this UI is the app's own.</sub></p>

## Why a separate client

The backend kits ([report-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-kit), [invoice-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/invoice-kit)) carry a PDF engine,
a native SVG renderer and fonts. A frontend needs none of that. This package is all a browser app installs:

- **Headless.** No components with styling, no CSS, no layout. Build any UI/UX.
- **Zero dependencies.** About 4 KB, plus about 3 KB of optional React hooks.
- **Typed.** Request and response types for every route, checked against the backend kits at build time.
- **Any frontend.** React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, plain JS, React Native. It only needs `fetch`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  UI["Your UI<br/>(forms, buttons, theme)"] --> C["@mgpl-diagnostics/client"]
  C -- "fetch /api/mgpl/*" --> B["Backend<br/>createMgplApi()"]
  B --> P["PDF / HTML / JSON"]
  P --> C
```

## Quick start

```bash
npm i @mgpl-diagnostics/client
```

```ts
import { createMgplClient, downloadBlob } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

const mgpl = createMgplClient({ baseUrl: "/api/mgpl" }); // or "https://api.your-lab.in/api/mgpl"

const pdf = await mgpl.reports.pdf({
  patient: { title: "Mrs", name: "Kavita Sharma", age: 32, sex: "Female", patientId: "MGPL1025" },
  tests: [{ template: "cbc", results: { hb: "10.8", wbc: "6700" } }],
});
downloadBlob(pdf, "MGPL1025.pdf");
```

## GraphQL: the whole backend

[mgpl-diagnostics/api](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/api) serves everything (sign-in, patients,
bookings, samples, results, billing, books, GST, receivables, settlements, cash and bank, documents) at
**one endpoint, `POST /graphql`**. `createMgplGraphQLClient` has a typed method for each of its 138
operations, with no GraphQL library: the operations are plain strings, validated against the server's
schema by the api's contract test.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  UI["Your UI"] --> G["createMgplGraphQLClient()"]
  G -- "POST /graphql<br/>Authorization: Bearer token" --> API["mgpl-diagnostics/api"]
  API --> K["auth · db · catalog · report · invoice · tally · finance kits"]
```

```ts
import { createMgplGraphQLClient, documentBlob, openBlob, MgplGraphQLError } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

const mgpl = createMgplGraphQLClient({ url: "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql" });

await mgpl.auth.login({ email: "desk@your-lab.in", password });  // access + refresh tokens, refreshed for you
const [hit] = await mgpl.catalog.search("cbc");
const patient = await mgpl.patients.register({ branchId, name: "Kavita Sharma", sex: "female", ageYears: 32 });
const { booking } = await mgpl.bookings.create({ branchId, patientId: patient.id, tests: [{ testCode: hit!.test.code! }] });
const invoice = await mgpl.invoices.issue({
  branchId, patientId: patient.id, bookingId: booking.id,
  items: [{ code: "CBC" }],                                     // name and MRP from the catalog
  payments: [{ amountPaise: 30000, mode: "upi" }],
});
openBlob(documentBlob(await mgpl.documents.invoice(invoice.id)));  // the PDF arrives as base64

try {
  await mgpl.periods.setLockDate({ upTo: "2026-09-30" });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof MgplGraphQLError && e.code === "FORBIDDEN") alert("Ask an accountant");
}
```

**Sessions work with any library.** `mgpl.session` is a framework-agnostic session manager: access and
refresh tokens, automatic single-flight refresh (across tabs too), device signals bound to the refresh
token, `subscribe` / `getSnapshot` for React, Vue, Svelte or Solid, `session.fetch` for Apollo, urql or
graphql-request, and `mgplQuery` / `mgplMutation` / `mgplFetcher` for TanStack Query and SWR. See
[docs/session.md](docs/session.md).

Namespaces: `auth`, `users`, `organization`, `catalog`, `patients`, `doctors`, `bookings`, `samples`,
`reports`, `invoices`, `books`, `gst`, `receivables`, `settlements`, `cash`, `bank`, `periods`, `exports`,
`documents`, plus `request(query, variables)` for a custom selection. Money is integer paise; days are
`"YYYY-MM-DD"`. Full list: [docs/graphql.md](docs/graphql.md). The types are flat in
`@mgpl-diagnostics/client/graphql`, or under the `Gql` namespace in the main entry.

## The SDK (report and invoice HTTP API)

The REST client below talks to `createMgplApi()` (invoice-kit) or `createReportApi()` (report-kit) when an
app mounts them directly, as report-studio does. New apps should use the GraphQL client above.


| Call | Backend route | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `mgpl.reports.templates()` | `GET /templates` | every test with its result fields + profiles |
| `mgpl.reports.pdf(req)` / `.html(req)` | `POST /report` | `Blob` (PDF) / `string` (HTML) |
| `mgpl.reports.letterheadPdf()` / `.letterheadHtml()` / `.letterheadUrl()` | `GET /letterhead` | stationery |
| `mgpl.reports.samples()` | `GET /samples` | demo reports (if enabled) |
| `mgpl.invoices.totals(invoice)` | `POST /invoice` (json) | totals, GST, status, amount in words |
| `mgpl.invoices.pdf(req)` / `.html(req)` | `POST /invoice` | `Blob` / `string` |
| `mgpl.invoices.priceList()` | `GET /price-list` | codes usable as invoice items |
| `mgpl.health()` | `GET /health` | `{ ok }` |

Browser helpers: `downloadBlob(blob, name)`, `openBlob(blob)`, `printBlob(blob)`.

**Build an entry form from the catalog.** Nothing about tests is hard-coded in your app:

```ts
const { templates } = await mgpl.reports.templates();
// templates[i] = { id: "cbc", name: "Complete Blood Count (CBC)", category: "Hematology",
//                  fields: [{ key: "hb", label: "Haemoglobin (HB)", unit: "g/dL", range: "12.0 - 15.0" }, …] }
```

## React (optional)

`@mgpl-diagnostics/client/react` adds **unstyled** hooks and one bare iframe. Pass your own `className`/`style`.

```tsx
"use client";
import { useRef } from "react";
import { createMgplClient } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";
import { HtmlFrame, useReportHtml, useTemplates, type HtmlFrameHandle } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client/react";

const mgpl = createMgplClient();

export function Preview({ request }) {
  const { data: html, loading, error } = useReportHtml(mgpl, request);
  const frame = useRef<HtmlFrameHandle>(null);
  if (error) return <p className="my-error">{error.message}</p>;
  return (
    <>
      <button className="my-button" onClick={() => frame.current?.print()}>Print</button>
      {html && <HtmlFrame ref={frame} html={html} className="my-paper" />}
    </>
  );
}
```

| Hook | Gives you |
|---|---|
| `useTemplates(client)` | the test catalog |
| `useReportHtml(client, req)` / `useInvoiceHtml(client, req)` | backend HTML, re-fetched when `req` changes |
| `useInvoiceTotals(client, invoice)` | live totals while an invoice is edited |
| `usePdfUrl(load, key)` | object URL of a PDF for `<iframe src>` / `<a download>` |
| `useAsync(load, key)` | the generic loader behind them all |

`HtmlFrame` isolates the document (its CSS can't touch yours), disables scripts, sizes itself to the content and
exposes `print()`.

## Errors and auth (HTTP API)

```ts
import { createMgplClient, MgplApiError } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

const mgpl = createMgplClient({
  baseUrl: "https://api.your-lab.in/api/mgpl",
  headers: async () => ({ Authorization: `Bearer ${await getToken()}` }), // added to every call
  credentials: "include",                                                // cookie auth across origins
});

try {
  await mgpl.reports.pdf({ tests: [] });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof MgplApiError) console.log(e.status, e.message); // 400 "patient needs name, age and sex"
}
```

For a backend on another origin, enable CORS there: `createMgplApi({ cors: "https://app.your-lab.in" })`.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm run build      # dist/index.js, dist/graphql.js, dist/react.js (the React entry is marked "use client")
```

End-to-end tests of the HTTP SDK against the real backend live in invoice-kit (`npm run test:api`). The
GraphQL operations are validated against the server's schema by mgpl-diagnostics/api (`npm test`).
Docs: [docs/graphql.md](docs/graphql.md) · [docs/api.md](docs/api.md) · [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) · AI index [llms.txt](llms.txt) / [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt).

## Part of MGPL Diagnostics

| Repo | Side | |
|---|---|---|
| [report-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-kit) | backend | reports, letterhead, templates |
| [invoice-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/invoice-kit) | backend | patient invoices + combined API |

## File: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — @mgpl-diagnostics/client

Instructions for AI coding agents and developers.

## What this is

The **frontend** SDK for the MGPL Diagnostics backend: the GraphQL API of **mgpl-diagnostics/api** (one
endpoint, `POST /graphql`, for everything) and the HTTP API of `createMgplApi()` (invoice-kit) /
`createReportApi()` (report-kit). It is **headless and has zero dependencies**: a typed `fetch` client,
browser helpers, and optional **unstyled** React hooks. All rendering (reports, invoices, PDFs) happens on
the backend. Apps build their own UI/UX on top.

## Rules

1. **No runtime dependencies.** Not even React in the main entry; React is an optional peer used only by `src/react.tsx`.
   `@mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit` is a dev dependency **bundled into dist** (`noExternal` in `tsup.config.ts`);
   public types must not import from it (`SignalSource` is structural).
2. **No UI.** No styled components, no CSS, no layout decisions. `HtmlFrame` is a bare iframe that
   accepts `className`/`style`. If you feel the need for a component with looks, it belongs in the app.
3. **The contract is mirrored, not imported.** `src/types.ts` mirrors report-kit's `src/shared/api.ts` /
   `types.ts` and invoice-kit's `api.ts`. Never import from the backend kits (that would pull the PDF
   engine into browsers). report-studio's `contract-check.ts` type-checks both sides; update them together.
4. **GraphQL operations are plain strings** in `src/graphql/operations.ts` (no GraphQL library). Their
   selections match `src/graphql/types.ts`. mgpl-diagnostics/api validates every operation against its
   schema and checks that every root field has one; when the API adds or renames a field, update
   `operations.ts`, `types.ts` and `client.ts` here, release, then bump the client ref in api's `kits.json`.
5. **Routes** are in `ROUTES` in `src/index.ts` and must match report-kit `src/shared/api.ts` + invoice-kit `INVOICE_ROUTES`.
6. **Sessions stay library-agnostic.** No data or state library is imported: adapters return plain objects
   and functions (`{ queryKey, queryFn }`, a `fetch`, `subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Device signals are listed in
   docs/session.md; collect nothing new without adding it there (no canvas, audio or font probing).
7. `src/react.tsx` gets a `"use client"` banner from tsup (see `tsup.config.ts`); the main entry must not,
   so it stays usable from Server Components, workers and Node scripts.

## Map

```
src/types.ts    contract types (Patient, ReportRequest, TemplateCatalog, InvoiceInput, InvoiceTotals, …)
src/index.ts    createMgplClient (reports.*, invoices.*, health, url), MgplApiError, ROUTES, downloadBlob/openBlob/printBlob
src/graphql/
  transport.ts  createTransport (POST, Bearer from the session, one refresh + retry on UNAUTHENTICATED), MgplGraphQLError
  session.ts    createSessionManager (tokens, single-flight refresh, Web Locks, subscribe/getSnapshot/store, fetch), storages
  device.ts     createDeviceCollector: maps @mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit's signals to DeviceInput (deviceId, clientSessionId, fingerprint, info)
  query.ts      mgplQuery / mgplMutation / mgplKey / mgplFetcher / clearOnSignOut (TanStack Query, SWR; no dependency)
  operations.ts FRAGMENTS + OPERATIONS (one per Query/Mutation field), withFragments
  client.ts     createMgplGraphQLClient (auth, users, organization, catalog, patients, … documents), documentBlob, csvBlob
  types.ts      the API's GraphQL types as selected by operations.ts, plus inputs
  index.ts      the "/graphql" entry (types flat); the main entry re-exports the client, types under `Gql`
src/react.tsx   useMgplSession, useAsync, useTemplates, useReportHtml, useInvoiceHtml, useInvoiceTotals, usePdfUrl, HtmlFrame
```

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm run build        # dist/index.js, dist/react.js (+ .d.ts)
```

End-to-end tests run in invoice-kit: `npm run test:api` drives this SDK against the real backend, over
an in-process handler and over a real `node:http` server.

## File: docs/api.md

# API reference: @mgpl-diagnostics/client

This page covers the HTTP client (`createMgplClient`) for report-kit / invoice-kit's API. The GraphQL
client for mgpl-diagnostics/api is in [graphql.md](graphql.md).

## createMgplClient(options?)

```ts
interface ClientOptions {
  baseUrl?: string;                     // default "/api/mgpl"
  fetch?: typeof fetch;                 // custom fetch (tests, SSR, retries)
  headers?: HeadersInit | (() => HeadersInit | Promise<HeadersInit>);   // e.g. auth
  credentials?: RequestCredentials;     // "include" for cookies across origins
}

const mgpl = createMgplClient(options);
mgpl.baseUrl;                    mgpl.url(path, query?)        mgpl.health()

mgpl.reports.templates(): Promise<TemplateCatalog>
mgpl.reports.samples(): Promise<SampleInfo[]>
mgpl.reports.pdf(req: ReportRequest): Promise<Blob>
mgpl.reports.html(req: ReportRequest): Promise<string>
mgpl.reports.letterheadPdf(): Promise<Blob>       .letterheadHtml(): Promise<string>       .letterheadUrl(download?)

mgpl.invoices.priceList(): Promise<PriceEntry[]>
mgpl.invoices.samples(): Promise<InvoiceSampleInfo[]>
mgpl.invoices.totals(invoice: InvoiceInput): Promise<InvoiceTotals>
mgpl.invoices.pdf(req: InvoiceRequest): Promise<Blob>
mgpl.invoices.html(req: InvoiceRequest): Promise<string>
```

Any non-2xx response throws `MgplApiError { status, message }` (the server's `error` text).

## Requests

```ts
interface ReportRequest {
  patient?: Patient; tests?: { template: string; results: Results }[];
  profile?: { id: string; results: Record<string, Results> }; sample?: string;
  variant?: "header" | "non-header"; design?: "sidebar" | "classic"; fileName?: string; download?: boolean;
}
type Results = Record<string, string | { value?: string; flag?: Flag; range?: string | string[]; unit?: string; method?: string } | string[] | undefined>

interface InvoiceRequest { invoice?: InvoiceInput; sample?: string; variant?: ReportVariant; fileName?: string; download?: boolean }
interface InvoiceInput {
  invoiceNo: string; date?: string; patient: Patient;
  items: (string | (Partial<InvoiceItem> & { code: string }) | InvoiceItem)[];
  discount?: { percent?: number; amount?: number; reason?: string };
  payments?: { mode: string; amount: number; date?: string; reference?: string }[];
  notes?: string[]; roundOff?: boolean; title?: string;
}
interface Patient {
  title?; name; age: number | string; ageUnit?; sex; patientId?; refDoctor?; sampleCollectionDate?;
  sampleId?; sampleType?; phone?; address?; collectedAt?; registeredAt?; reportedAt?;
}
```

## Responses

`TemplateCatalog { templates: { id, name, category?, specimen?, method?, fields: { key, label, unit?, range? }[] }[], profiles: { id, name, tests }[] }`

`InvoiceTotals { lines[], subtotal, lineDiscount, billDiscount, taxable, tax, taxByRate[], roundOff, total, paid, due, excess, status, hasTax, hasDiscount, amountInWords }`

`PriceEntry { code, name, category, rate, taxPercent?, hsn? }`

## Browser helpers

`downloadBlob(blob, fileName)` · `openBlob(blob)` · `printBlob(blob)`

## React (`@mgpl-diagnostics/client/react`, unstyled)

```ts
useAsync<T>(load: () => Promise<T>, key: string): { data, loading, error, reload }
useTemplates(client)
useReportHtml(client, req | null)     useInvoiceHtml(client, req | null)
useInvoiceTotals(client, invoice | null)
usePdfUrl(load | null, key): { …, url }
<HtmlFrame html autoHeight? className? style? ref={HtmlFrameHandle} />   // HtmlFrameHandle.print()
```

## File: docs/graphql.md

# GraphQL client: @mgpl-diagnostics/client

`createMgplGraphQLClient` talks to **mgpl-diagnostics/api**, the backend that serves everything at one
endpoint (`POST /graphql`). It has no dependencies: every operation is a plain string in
`src/graphql/operations.ts`, and the api's test suite validates each one against the server's schema.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant App as Your app
  participant C as createMgplGraphQLClient
  participant API as api (POST /graphql)
  App->>C: auth.login({ email, password })
  C->>API: mutation Login (+ device signals)
  API-->>C: { accessToken, refreshToken, user }
  C->>C: session.signIn(…)
  App->>C: invoices.issue({...})
  C->>API: mutation IssueInvoice (Authorization: Bearer accessToken, refreshed first when it expires)
  API-->>C: data.issueInvoice
  C-->>App: Invoice
```

Tokens, automatic refresh, device signals and use with TanStack Query, SWR, Apollo, urql or any other
library: [session.md](session.md).

## Options

```ts
createMgplGraphQLClient({
  url?: string;                    // default "/graphql"
  fetch?: typeof fetch;            // tests, SSR, retry wrappers
  session?: SessionManager;        // tokens + refresh + device signals (default: one in memory)
  device?: DeviceCollector | false; // for the default session manager
  token?: string | null;           // starting access token
  onToken?: (token: string | null) => void; // called when the access token changes
  headers?: HeadersInit | (() => HeadersInit | Promise<HeadersInit>);
  credentials?: RequestCredentials;
});
```

The client keeps the tokens in its session manager (`client.session`). `auth.login` fills it,
`auth.logout` ends the session on the server and clears it, and requests refresh the access token by
themselves. See [session.md](session.md).

## Conventions

- **Money is integer paise** (`totalPaise: 35400` is Rs 354.00). Catalog `mrp` and `priceList().rate` are rupees.
- **DateTime** is an ISO string; **Day** is `"YYYY-MM-DD"` in IST. The financial year runs April to March (`"2026-27"`).
- **Lists** take `limit` / `offset`; the server caps `limit` at 200.
- **Documents** come back as `{ format, fileName, mimeType, byteLength, base64, html }`: a PDF in `base64`,
  HTML (self-contained, fonts inlined) in `html`. `documentBlob(doc)` turns either into a Blob for
  `downloadBlob`, `openBlob` or `printBlob`. CSV exports come as `{ fileName, mimeType, content }`; use `csvBlob(file)`.
- The organisation and the acting user always come from the session. No method takes an `orgId`.

## Errors

Every failure throws `MgplGraphQLError` with a stable `code`:

| code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | No token, or it expired. Sign in again. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | The user lacks the permission (at that branch). |
| `NOT_FOUND` | The id does not exist in this organisation. |
| `BAD_USER_INPUT` | Validation failed; `message` says what. |
| `CONFLICT` | Duplicate or wrong state (e.g. releasing an unverified report). |
| `PERIOD_LOCKED` | The date is on or before a lock date. |
| `CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | A customer invoice would exceed the credit limit. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, `INVITE_PENDING`, `ORG_REQUIRED`, `RATE_LIMITED` (with `extensions.retryAfterMs`), `WEAK_PASSWORD`, `INVALID_TOKEN` | auth-kit's codes, unchanged. |
| `NETWORK_ERROR` / `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | No response, or a server fault (details are masked). |

`error.errors` holds every GraphQL error, `error.status` the HTTP status, `error.data` any partial data.

## Custom selections

The typed methods select a fixed set of fields. For anything else, send your own document:

```ts
const data = await mgpl.request<{ patient: { name: string; invoices: { invoiceNo: string; duePaise: number }[] } }>(
  `query ($id: ID!) { patient(id: $id) { name invoices(limit: 5) { invoiceNo duePaise } } }`,
  { id },
);
```

`OPERATIONS[name].document` and `FRAGMENTS` are exported too, for GraphQL tools that want the strings.

## Methods

Each method runs one operation and returns its root field. Permissions are listed in the api's
docs (`docs/04-api-reference.md`).

### client (root)

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `health` | query `health` |
| `ping` | mutation `ping` |

### auth

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `login` | mutation `login` (adds device signals) |
| `refresh` | mutation `refreshSession` (also automatic) |
| `logout` | mutation `logout` (by refresh token) |
| `viewer` | query `viewer` |
| `can` | query `viewer { can }` |
| `sessions` | query `mySessions` |
| `logoutOtherSessions` | mutation `logoutOtherSessions` |
| `revokeSession` | mutation `revokeSession` |
| `changePassword` | mutation `changePassword` |
| `requestPasswordReset` | mutation `requestPasswordReset` |
| `resetPassword` | mutation `resetPassword` |

### users

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `list` | query `users` |
| `get` | query `user` |
| `create` | mutation `createUser` |
| `setRoles` | mutation `setUserRoles` |
| `disable` | mutation `disableUser` |
| `enable` | mutation `enableUser` |
| `setPassword` | mutation `setUserPassword` |
| `roles` | query `roles` |
| `upsertRole` | mutation `upsertRole` |
| `permissions` | query `permissions` |

### organization

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `get` | query `organization` |
| `update` | mutation `updateOrganization` |
| `branches` | query `branches` |
| `branch` | query `branch` |
| `createBranch` | mutation `createBranch` |
| `updateBranch` | mutation `updateBranch` |
| `auditLog` | query `auditLog` |

### catalog

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `search` | query `catalogSearch` |
| `test` | query `catalogTest` |
| `tests` | query `catalogTests` |
| `departments` | query `catalogDepartments` |
| `sampleTypes` | query `catalogSampleTypes` |
| `priceQuote` | query `priceQuote` |

### patients

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `search` | query `patients` |
| `get` | query `patient` |
| `register` | mutation `registerPatient` |
| `update` | mutation `updatePatient` |

### doctors

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `list` | query `doctors` |
| `create` | mutation `createDoctor` |
| `update` | mutation `updateDoctor` |

### bookings

| Method | GraphQL |
|---|---|
| `list` | query `bookings` |
| `get` | query `booking` |
| `create` | mutation `createBooking` |
| `cancel` | mutation `cancelBooking` |

### samples

| Method | GraphQL |

## File: docs/session.md

# Sessions, tokens and device signals

The API signs users in with **two tokens**:

- a short-lived **access token**: a JWT sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, 15 minutes by default;
- a long-lived, single-use **refresh token**, which buys the next pair (`refreshSession`).

The SDK's **session manager** handles them for you, with no dependency and no framework:

- it keeps the tokens in memory by default, or in storage you choose;
- it refreshes shortly before the access token expires, and once more if a request comes back
  `UNAUTHENTICATED`;
- one refresh at a time: parallel requests share it, and so do tabs (Web Locks);
- it tells any UI library when the session changes;
- it sends **device signals** with login and refresh, so the server can bind the refresh token to the device.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as Your UI (any library)
  participant S as session manager
  participant API as api (POST /graphql)
  UI->>S: client.auth.login({ email, password })
  S->>API: login(input + device)
  API-->>S: accessToken (15 min) + refreshToken
  S-->>UI: snapshot { status: signed_in, user }
  UI->>API: queries (Bearer accessToken)
  Note over S: access token expires in < 30 s
  S->>API: refreshSession(refreshToken, device) — once, shared by every caller and tab
  API-->>S: new accessToken + new refreshToken (old one spent)
  UI->>API: a request comes back UNAUTHENTICATED
  S->>API: refresh, then retry the request once
  API-->>S: INVALID_TOKEN (spent, expired, other device)
  S-->>UI: snapshot { status: signed_out }, onSignedOut("refresh_failed")
```

## Setup

```ts
import { createMgplGraphQLClient, createSessionManager, webSessionStorage } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

// default: tokens in memory (lost on reload; safest against XSS)
const mgpl = createMgplGraphQLClient({ url: "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql" });

// or: survive reloads and sync tabs (localStorage is readable by any script on the page)
const session = createSessionManager({
  url: "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql",
  storage: webSessionStorage(),            // or memorySessionStorage(), or your own SessionStorage
  onSignedOut: (reason) => router.push("/login"),
});
const mgpl2 = createMgplGraphQLClient({ url: "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql", session });

await mgpl2.auth.login({ email, password });   // device signals are added for you
await mgpl2.auth.logout();                     // ends the server session (by refresh token), clears storage
```

`SessionStorage` is `{ get(), set(value), subscribe?(listener) }`. On React Native, implement it on
SecureStore or Keychain; in Electron, on safeStorage.

| Session manager | |
| --- | --- |
| `getSnapshot()` / `subscribe(listener)` | `{ status, user, accessExpiresAt, refreshExpiresAt }`; same object until it changes |
| `store` | Svelte-style readable store |
| `accessToken()` | a valid access token (refreshed first when needed) or null |
| `refresh()` | single-flight refresh; true when it worked |
| `signIn(result)` / `signOut(reason?)` / `current()` | keep, forget or read the tokens |
| `headers()` | `{ authorization }` for clients that take a headers function |
| `fetch` | a fetch that adds the token and refreshes and retries once on `UNAUTHENTICATED` |
| `device()` | the device signals |

Options: `url`, `fetch`, `storage`, `device` (a collector, or `false`), `refreshMarginMs` (default 30 s),
`headers`, `onSignedOut`.

## Any UI or data library

```tsx
// React
import { useMgplSession } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client/react";
const { status, user } = useMgplSession(mgpl.session);   // useSyncExternalStore underneath

// Svelte
{#if $store.status === "signed_in"} … {/if}               // const store = mgpl.session.store

// Vue
const s = shallowRef(mgpl.session.getSnapshot());
onScopeDispose(mgpl.session.subscribe((v) => (s.value = v)));
```

### TanStack Query (React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Angular)

```ts
import { mgplQuery, mgplMutation, mgplKey, clearOnSignOut } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

const invoices = useQuery(mgplQuery(mgpl, "invoices", { limit: 20 }));       // { queryKey, queryFn }
const issue = useMutation({ ...mgplMutation(mgpl, "issueInvoice"), onSuccess: () => qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["mgpl", "invoices"] }) });
clearOnSignOut(mgpl.session, qc);                                             // no cached data after logout
```

Keys are `["mgpl", operationName, variables]`; invalidate `["mgpl"]` to refetch everything. Typed
methods work too: `queryFn: () => mgpl.invoices.list({ limit: 20 })`.

### SWR, RTK Query, Apollo, urql, graphql-request

```ts
useSWR(mgplKey("invoices", { limit: 20 }), mgplFetcher(mgpl));                // SWR
new HttpLink({ uri: "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql", fetch: session.fetch }); // Apollo
createClient({ url: "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql", fetch: session.fetch, exchanges: [fetchExchange] }); // urql
new GraphQLClient(url, { fetch: session.fetch });                            // graphql-request
fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl, fetchFn: session.fetch });                          // RTK Query
```

## Device signals

Login and refresh carry `device: { deviceId, fingerprint, clientSessionId, info }`. The server stores
them on the session. A refresh from **another `deviceId` ends the session** (`DEVICE_BINDING=enforce`,
the default), so a stolen refresh token does not work elsewhere. A changed fingerprint is only logged,
because browser updates change it.

| Signal | What it is | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deviceId` | random id, created once | `localStorage` key `mgpl.deviceId` (memory where unavailable) |
| `clientSessionId` | random id per tab or app run | `sessionStorage` key `mgpl.tabId` |
| `fingerprint` | SHA-256 (32 hex characters) of OS, browser family, mobile, platform, language, time zone, screen size, colour depth, CPU cores, device memory and touch points; the browser version is left out so updates don't change it | WebCrypto |
| `info` | `os`, `browser`, `browserVersion` (major only), `mobile`, `language`, `timezone`, `screen`, plus your `extraInfo` | `navigator`, `screen`, `Intl` |

The values are collected by [security-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit)
(`@mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit/browser`), which is bundled into this package, so the SDK still has no
runtime dependency. Devices that signed in before 1.3.0 keep their `deviceId`.

Nothing else is read: no canvas, audio, font or IP probing, and no third-party script. Tell your users
in your privacy notice that these values are used to keep their account secure.

```ts
import { createDeviceCollector } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

const device = createDeviceCollector({
  store: secureStoreAdapter,                                      // React Native: keep the id in SecureStore
  extraInfo: () => ({ appVersion: "2.3.0", model: Device.modelName }),
  exclude: ["screen"],
});
const session = createSessionManager({ url, device });             // or device: false to send none
```

To share one collector with the rest of your app (for example security-kit's `signalFetch` or
`useDeviceSignals`), pass it in:

```ts
import { createSignalCollector } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit/browser";

const signals = createSignalCollector({ app: "lab-panel@1.4.0" });
const device = createDeviceCollector({ signals }); // the session manager sends the same ids
```

## File: llms.txt

# @mgpl-diagnostics/client

> Headless, zero-dependency TypeScript SDK for browsers (or any fetch runtime) that talks to the MGPL Diagnostics backend (`createMgplApi` / `createReportApi`). It requests lab reports and invoices as PDF Blobs, HTML strings or JSON, and fetches the test catalog and price list. It has no UI and no CSS; apps build their own UI/UX. Optional unstyled React hooks live in "@mgpl-diagnostics/client/react".

Key facts for agents:
- GraphQL (mgpl-diagnostics/api, one endpoint for everything): `const mgpl = createMgplGraphQLClient({ url: "/graphql", session? })`; `await mgpl.auth.login({ email, password })` keeps the tokens. Namespaces: auth, users, organization, catalog, patients, doctors, bookings, samples, reports, invoices, books, gst, receivables, settlements, cash, bank, periods, exports, documents; `request(query, vars)` for custom selections. Errors throw `MgplGraphQLError` with `code`. Money in paise; documents are base64 PDFs or HTML (`documentBlob`). Types flat in "@mgpl-diagnostics/client/graphql" or under `Gql`.
- Sessions (any library): `mgpl.session` (or `createSessionManager({ url, storage: webSessionStorage() | memorySessionStorage(), device?, onSignedOut? })` passed as `session`) keeps access + refresh tokens, refreshes once (single flight, Web Locks across tabs), retries once on UNAUTHENTICATED, sends device signals (`createDeviceCollector`: deviceId, clientSessionId, fingerprint, info). `subscribe`/`getSnapshot`/`store` for React (`useMgplSession`), Vue, Svelte; `session.fetch` for Apollo/urql/graphql-request; `mgplQuery`/`mgplMutation`/`mgplKey`/`mgplFetcher`/`clearOnSignOut` for TanStack Query and SWR. Background documents: `documents.startJob`, `job`, `waitForJob`.
- `const mgpl = createMgplClient({ baseUrl: "/api/mgpl", headers?, credentials?, fetch? })`.
- Reports: `mgpl.reports.templates()`, `.pdf(req)`, `.html(req)`, `.letterheadPdf()`, `.samples()`. Invoices: `mgpl.invoices.totals(invoice)`, `.pdf(req)`, `.html(req)`, `.priceList()`.
- Build entry forms from `templates()`: each template lists `fields` (key, label, unit, range); send `{ patient, tests: [{ template, results: { [key]: value } }] }`.
- Errors throw `MgplApiError` (status + server message). Helpers: downloadBlob, openBlob, printBlob.
- React: useTemplates, useReportHtml, useInvoiceHtml, useInvoiceTotals, usePdfUrl, useAsync, and `<HtmlFrame html />` (bare sandboxed iframe with `.print()`).
- Never import the backend kits here. The types in src/types.ts mirror them and are checked by report-studio's contract-check.ts.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): why, quick start, SDK table, React hooks, errors and auth
- [GraphQL client](docs/graphql.md): every method, the operation it runs, errors, conventions

- [API reference](docs/api.md): every method, option and type
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules (no deps, no UI, mirrored contract)
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): everything above plus the source

## File: scripts/llms-full.mjs

````js
// Builds llms-full.txt: every doc and source file of the repo in one plain-text document for AI tools.
//   node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> [file-or-folder …]
// Folders are walked recursively. Output order: README, AGENTS, docs, then the rest alphabetically.
// Skipped: build output, dependencies, lockfiles, generated files, binaries. Files over 150 KB are
// listed (path + size) instead of inlined. CI checks the file is up to date (`npm run llms` + git diff).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join, relative } from "node:path";

const [title, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!title || !inputs.length) {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> …');
  process.exit(1);
}

const TEXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".md", ".mdx", ".json", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".txt", ".graphql", ".gql", ".sql", ".html"]);
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(["node_modules", "dist", ".next", ".git", ".turbo", "coverage", "examples", ".pg-test"]);
const SKIP_FILES = /(^|\/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock|llms-full\.txt|[^/]*\.generated\.[^/]+|[^/]*\.log)$/;
const MAX = 150 * 1024;
const LANG = { ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".mts": "ts", ".cts": "ts", ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".json": "json", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml", ".graphql": "graphql", ".gql": "graphql", ".sql": "sql", ".html": "html" };

const posix = (p) => p.split("\\").join("/");
const files = new Set();
function walk(p) {
  const st = statSync(p);
  if (st.isDirectory()) {
    for (const name of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) walk(join(p, name));
  } else if (TEXT.has(extname(p).toLowerCase()) && !SKIP_FILES.test(posix(p))) {
    files.add(posix(relative(".", p)));
  }
}
for (const input of inputs) walk(input);

const rank = (f) => (/^README\.md$/i.test(f) ? 0 : /^AGENTS\.md$/i.test(f) ? 1 : /^docs\//.test(f) ? 2 : 3);
const ordered = [...files].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));

const parts = [`# ${title} — full documentation and source\n\n> Generated by scripts/llms-full.mjs. Do not edit by hand. ${ordered.length} files.\n\n## Contents\n\n${ordered.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n")}\n`];
const omitted = [];
for (const f of ordered) {
  // LF-normalised text, so Windows and Linux checkouts produce byte-identical output
  const body = readFileSync(f, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  const size = Buffer.byteLength(body);
  if (size > MAX) {
    omitted.push(`${f} (${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB)`);
    parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n_Omitted: ${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB. Read the file directly._\n`);
    continue;
  }
  const lang = LANG[extname(f).toLowerCase()];
  const fence = body.includes("```") ? "````" : "```";
  parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n${lang ? `${fence}${lang}\n${body}\n${fence}` : body}\n`);
}
const out = parts.join("");
writeFileSync("llms-full.txt", out);
console.log(`llms-full.txt: ${ordered.length} files, ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB${omitted.length ? `; omitted (too large): ${omitted.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
````

## File: src/graphql/client.ts

```ts
// createMgplGraphQLClient: one typed method per operation of the backend's single GraphQL endpoint
// (mgpl-diagnostics/api, POST /graphql). Zero dependencies: operations are plain strings.
import type { InvoiceRequest, InvoiceTotals, ReportRequest } from "../types";
import { OPERATIONS, type Operation } from "./operations";
import { createDeviceCollector, type DeviceCollector } from "./device";
import { createSessionManager, memorySessionStorage } from "./session";
import { createTransport, type GraphQLClientOptions, type Variables } from "./transport";
import type * as T from "./types";

type Page = { limit?: number; offset?: number };
type Range = { from: T.DateTime; to: T.DateTime };
type Csv = { bom?: boolean };

export interface MgplGraphQLClientOptions extends GraphQLClientOptions {
  /** Device signals for the default session manager (ignored when you pass `session`). false: none. */
  device?: DeviceCollector | false;
}

export function createMgplGraphQLClient(opts: MgplGraphQLClientOptions = {}) {
  const session =
    opts.session ??
    createSessionManager({
      url: opts.url,
      fetch: opts.fetch,
      storage: memorySessionStorage(opts.token ? { accessToken: opts.token } : null),
      device: opts.device === false ? false : (opts.device ?? createDeviceCollector()),
    });
  if (opts.onToken) {
    let last = session.current()?.accessToken ?? null;
    session.subscribe(() => {
      const t = session.current()?.accessToken ?? null;
      if (t !== last) opts.onToken!((last = t));
    });
  }
  const transport = createTransport({ ...opts, session });

  /** Runs one operation and returns its root field. */
  async function run<R>(operation: Operation, variables?: Variables, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<R> {
    const data = await transport.request<Record<string, unknown>>(operation.document, variables, { signal });
    return data[operation.field] as R;
  }
  const O = OPERATIONS;

  return {
    url: transport.url,
    /** Any query or mutation, for what the typed methods don't cover (e.g. a custom selection). */
    request: transport.request,
    getToken: transport.getToken,
    setToken: transport.setToken,
    /** Tokens, refresh, device signals and change events: share it with any UI or data library. */
    session,

    health: () => run<T.Health>(O.health),
    ping: () => run<string>(O.ping),

    auth: {
      /** Signs in (with this device's signals) and keeps the tokens in the session manager. */
      async login(input: T.LoginInput): Promise<T.LoginResult> {
        const device = input.device ?? (await session.device());
        const result = await run<T.LoginResult>(O.login, { input: { ...input, device } });
        session.signIn(result);
        return result;
      },
      /** Trades the refresh token for new tokens now (the client also does it by itself when needed). */
      refresh: () => session.refresh(),
      /** Ends this session on the server (by its refresh token, so an expired access token is fine) and forgets the tokens. */
      async logout(): Promise<void> {
        const cur = session.current();
        try {
          if (cur) await transport.request(O.logout.document, { refreshToken: cur.refreshToken ?? undefined });
        } catch {
          /* already ended on the server */
        } finally {
          session.signOut("logout");
        }
      },
      /** The signed-in user, organisation and permissions; null when the token is missing or expired. */
      viewer: () => run<T.Viewer | null>(O.viewer),
      /** Whether the signed-in user may do `permission` (at `branchId`, when given). */
      can: async (permission: string, branchId?: T.ID) =>
        (await run<{ can: boolean } | null>(O.can, { permission, branchId }))?.can ?? false,
      sessions: () => run<T.Session[]>(O.mySessions),

      /** Always resolves true; the server emails the link if the account exists. */
      requestPasswordReset: (email: string, orgCode?: string) => run<boolean>(O.requestPasswordReset, { email, orgCode }),
      resetPassword: (token: string, newPassword: string) => run<boolean>(O.resetPassword, { token, newPassword }),

    /** Reports and invoices rendered by the server (report-kit / invoice-kit). PDFs come as base64. */
    documents: {
      templates: () => run<T.ReportTemplateCatalog>(O.reportTemplates),
      priceList: () => run<T.PriceListEntry[]>(O.priceList),

        run<T.RenderedDocument>(O.renderInvoice, { request, ...o }),
      /** invoice-kit's calculation, without rendering (amounts in rupees). */
      invoiceTotals: (request: InvoiceRequest) => run<InvoiceTotals>(O.invoiceTotals, { request }),
      letterhead: (format?: T.DocumentFormat) => run<T.RenderedDocument>(O.letterhead, { format }),
      /** A stored invoice, printed. */
      invoice: (invoiceId: T.ID, o: Omit<T.RenderOptions, "design" | "fileName"> = {}) =>
        run<T.RenderedDocument>(O.invoiceDocument, { invoiceId, ...o }),
      /** A booking's verified or released reports printed together (or only `reportIds`). */
      bookingReports: (bookingId: T.ID, o: Omit<T.RenderOptions, "fileName"> & { reportIds?: T.ID[] } = {}) =>
        run<T.RenderedDocument>(O.bookingReportDocument, { bookingId, ...o }),
      /** Renders a stored invoice or a booking's reports in the background worker. */
      startJob: (input: T.DocumentJobInput) => run<T.Job>(O.startDocumentJob, { input }),
      /** A job you started; null when unknown or expired. */
      job: (id: T.ID) => run<T.Job | null>(O.job, { id }),
      /** Polls a job until it is completed (returns it) or failed (throws). */
      async waitForJob(id: T.ID, o: { intervalMs?: number; timeoutMs?: number; signal?: AbortSignal } = {}): Promise<T.Job> {
        const end = Date.now() + (o.timeoutMs ?? 120_000);
        for (;;) {
          const job = await run<T.Job | null>(O.job, { id }, o.signal);
          if (!job) throw new Error(`Job ${id} not found`);
          if (job.state === "completed") return job;
          if (job.state === "failed") throw new Error(job.error ?? "Job failed");
          if (Date.now() > end) throw new Error(`Job ${id} is still ${job.state}`);
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, o.intervalMs ?? 1000));
          o.signal?.throwIfAborted();
        }
      },
    },
  };
}

export type MgplGraphQLClient = ReturnType<typeof createMgplGraphQLClient>;

/** A rendered document as a Blob: PDF from base64, HTML from its markup. Use with downloadBlob/openBlob/printBlob. */
export function documentBlob(doc: Pick<T.RenderedDocument, "mimeType" | "base64" | "html">): Blob {
  if (doc.base64 != null) {
    const bin = atob(doc.base64);
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) bytes[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
    return new Blob([bytes], { type: doc.mimeType });
  }
  return new Blob([doc.html ?? ""], { type: doc.mimeType });
}

/** A CSV export as a Blob (UTF-8). */
export function csvBlob(file: T.CsvFile): Blob {
  return new Blob([file.content], { type: file.mimeType });
}

## File: src/graphql/device.ts

```ts
// Device signals for login and refresh, collected by @mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit (bundled into this
// package at build time, so the SDK keeps zero runtime dependencies). This module maps security-kit's
// signals to the API's DeviceInput; the GraphQL contract is unchanged.
// Works in browsers, React Native, workers and Node: every source is optional and feature-detected.
//
// What is collected (and nothing else):
//   deviceId         random id created once, kept in localStorage (or your store): NOT derived from the device
//   clientSessionId  random id per tab (sessionStorage) or per app run
//   fingerprint      SHA-256 (32 hex) of coarse attributes: OS, browser family, mobile, platform, language,
//                    timezone, screen size, colour depth, CPU cores, device memory, touch points
//   info             os, browser, browserVersion (major), mobile, language, timezone, screen
//                    (no canvas, audio or font probing, no full user agent)
import {
  createSignalCollector,
  deviceInfo as signalDeviceInfo,
  randomId as signalRandomId,
  toBase64Url,
  webStorage,
} from "@mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit/browser";

export interface DeviceSignals {
  deviceId?: string;
  fingerprint?: string;
  clientSessionId?: string;
  info?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;
}

/** Where the device id and tab id live. Defaults: localStorage / sessionStorage when present, else memory. */
export interface DeviceStore {
  get(key: string): string | null | undefined | Promise<string | null | undefined>;
  set(key: string, value: string): void | Promise<void>;
  remove?(key: string): void | Promise<void>;
}

/**
 * A security-kit collector (`createSignalCollector` from "@mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit/browser"), to
 * share one collector between this SDK and the rest of the app. Only the parts used here.
 */
export interface SignalSource {
  collect(): Promise<{
    deviceId: string;
    tabId: string;
    fingerprint: string;
    device: { os: string; browser: string; browserVersion: string; mobile: boolean; language: string; timezone: string; screen: string };
    app?: string;
  }>;
}

export interface DeviceOptions {
  /** Keeps the device id (default: localStorage, else memory: a new id per run). */
  store?: DeviceStore;
  /** Keeps the per-tab id (default: sessionStorage, else memory). */
  tabStore?: DeviceStore;
  /** Your own values (app version, native device model, …); merged into `info`. */
  extraInfo?: () => Record<string, string | number | boolean> | Promise<Record<string, string | number | boolean>>;
  /** Leave values out of `info`, e.g. ["screen"]. */
  exclude?: string[];
  /** Use this security-kit collector instead of creating one (`store` / `tabStore` are then ignored). */
  signals?: SignalSource;
}

export interface DeviceCollector {
  /** The signals, collected once and cached (the tab id is stable for the tab's life). */
  get(): Promise<DeviceSignals>;
}

/** A random URL-safe id (128 bits, base64url). */
export function randomId(prefix = ""): string {
  return prefix + signalRandomId();
}

/** The descriptive values sent as `info` (security-kit's coarse device info). */
export function deviceInfo(): Record<string, string | number | boolean> {
  return { ...signalDeviceInfo() };
}

/** SHA-256 of the info values, base64url (43 characters); undefined where WebCrypto is missing. */
export async function fingerprintOf(info: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): Promise<string | undefined> {
  const subtle = (globalThis as { crypto?: Crypto }).crypto?.subtle;
  if (!subtle || typeof TextEncoder === "undefined") return undefined;
  const text = JSON.stringify(Object.keys(info).sort().map((k) => [k, info[k]]));
  return toBase64Url(new Uint8Array(await subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(text))));
}

/** Collects the signals the SDK sends with login and refresh. */
export function createDeviceCollector(o: DeviceOptions = {}): DeviceCollector {
  // same storage keys as before (mgpl.deviceId, mgpl.tabId), so existing devices keep their ids
  const signals = o.signals ?? createSignalCollector({ storage: o.store ?? webStorage("local"), tabStorage: o.tabStore ?? webStorage("session") });
  let cached: Promise<DeviceSignals> | undefined;
  return {
    get() {
      return (cached ??= (async () => {
        const s = await signals.collect();
        const info: Record<string, string | number | boolean> = { ...s.device, ...(s.app ? { app: s.app } : {}), ...((await o.extraInfo?.()) ?? {}) };
        for (const k of o.exclude ?? []) delete info[k];
        return { deviceId: s.deviceId, clientSessionId: s.tabId, fingerprint: s.fingerprint, info };
      })().catch((e) => {
        cached = undefined;
        throw e;
      }));
    },
  };
}
```

## File: src/graphql/operations.ts

```ts
// Every operation the client sends, as plain GraphQL strings (no runtime GraphQL library).
// The selections match src/graphql/types.ts. The API's contract test validates each one against
// the server's schema (mgpl-diagnostics/api, test/client-contract.ts), so a renamed field fails there.

/** Reusable selections. An operation gets the fragments it spreads (and theirs) appended. */
export const FRAGMENTS: Record<string, string> = {
  AddressFields: `fragment AddressFields on Address { line1 line2 city district state pincode }`,
  BranchRef: `fragment BranchRef on Branch { id code name }`,
  UserFields: `fragment UserFields on User { id name email phone status roles { role branchId } lastLoginAt createdAt }`,
  RoleFields: `fragment RoleFields on Role { id key name permissions system }`,

/** Appends every fragment the document spreads, transitively, once each. */
export function withFragments(doc: string): string {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const queue = [doc];
  while (queue.length) {
    for (const m of queue.pop()!.matchAll(/\.\.\.\s*([A-Z]\w*)/g)) {
      const name = m[1]!;
      if (seen.has(name) || !FRAGMENTS[name]) continue;
      seen.add(name);
      queue.push(FRAGMENTS[name]);
    }
  }
  return [doc, ...[...seen].map((n) => FRAGMENTS[n])].join("\n");
}

export interface Operation {
  /** The root field whose value the client returns. */
  field: string;
  document: string;
}

/**
 * One root field per operation. `vars` declares the variables ("$id: ID!, $limit: Int"); each one is
 * passed to the field under the same name. Omitted variables fall back to the schema's defaults.
 */
function op(kind: "query" | "mutation", field: string, vars: string, selection: string): Operation {
  const names = [...vars.matchAll(/\$(\w+)\s*:/g)].map((m) => m[1]!);
  const decl = vars ? `(${vars})` : "";
  const args = names.length ? `(${names.map((n) => `${n}: $${n}`).join(", ")})` : "";
  const name = field[0]!.toUpperCase() + field.slice(1);
  const body = selection ? ` { ${selection} }` : "";
  return { field, document: withFragments(`${kind} ${name}${decl} { ${field}${args}${body} }`) };
}
const q = (field: string, vars: string, selection = "") => op("query", field, vars, selection);
const m = (field: string, vars: string, selection = "") => op("mutation", field, vars, selection);

const PAGE = "$limit: Int, $offset: Int";
const RANGE = "$from: DateTime!, $to: DateTime!";
const CSV = "$bom: Boolean";

---

## File: src/graphql/query.ts

```ts
// Helpers for data-fetching libraries, with no dependency on any of them. They return plain objects
// and functions that fit TanStack Query (React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Angular), SWR, RTK Query, or your own.
//
//   TanStack Query:  useQuery(mgplQuery(client, "invoices", { limit: 20 }))
//                    useMutation(mgplMutation(client, "issueInvoice"))
//                    clearOnSignOut(client.session, queryClient)
//   SWR:             useSWR(mgplKey("invoices", { limit: 20 }), mgplFetcher(client))
import { OPERATIONS, type OperationName } from "./operations";
import type { SessionManager } from "./session";
import type { Variables } from "./transport";

/** What these helpers need from the GraphQL client. */
export interface RequestClient {
  request<T = unknown>(query: string, variables?: Variables, init?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<T>;
}

/** The cache key of an operation: ["mgpl", name, variables]. Invalidate ["mgpl"] to refetch everything. */
export const mgplKey = (name: OperationName, variables: Variables = {}) => ["mgpl", name, variables] as const;

/** Runs an operation by name and returns its root field. */
export async function runOperation<R = unknown>(client: RequestClient, name: OperationName, variables?: Variables, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<R> {
  const op = OPERATIONS[name];
  const data = await client.request<Record<string, unknown>>(op.document, variables, { signal });
  return data[op.field] as R;
}

/** `{ queryKey, queryFn }` for any query-style library (TanStack Query's useQuery / queryOptions). */
export function mgplQuery<R = unknown>(client: RequestClient, name: OperationName, variables: Variables = {}) {
  return {
    queryKey: mgplKey(name, variables),
    queryFn: ({ signal }: { signal?: AbortSignal } = {}) => runOperation<R>(client, name, variables, signal),
  };
}

/** `{ mutationKey, mutationFn }` (TanStack Query's useMutation). */
export function mgplMutation<R = unknown, V extends Variables = Variables>(client: RequestClient, name: OperationName) {
  return { mutationKey: ["mgpl", name] as const, mutationFn: (variables: V) => runOperation<R>(client, name, variables) };
}

/** A fetcher for key-based libraries (SWR): key = mgplKey(name, variables). */
export const mgplFetcher =
  (client: RequestClient) =>
  <R = unknown>(key: readonly [string, OperationName, Variables?]) =>
    runOperation<R>(client, key[1], key[2]);

/** Clears a query cache (anything with `clear()`, e.g. TanStack's QueryClient) when the session ends. */
export function clearOnSignOut(session: SessionManager, cache: { clear(): void }): () => void {
  let was = session.getSnapshot().status;
  return session.subscribe((s) => {
    if (was === "signed_in" && s.status === "signed_out") cache.clear();
    was = s.status;
  });
}
```

## File: src/graphql/session.ts

```ts
// The session manager: keeps the access and refresh tokens, refreshes them before they expire (once,
// even with many tabs and parallel requests), and tells any UI library when the session changes.
// Framework-agnostic and dependency-free:
//   - React:            useSyncExternalStore(session.subscribe, session.getSnapshot)  (or useMgplSession)
//   - Svelte:           session.store is a readable store ($session.store)
//   - Vue / Solid / …:  session.subscribe(snapshot => …)
//   - TanStack Query, SWR: see "./query"
//   - Apollo, urql, graphql-request, plain fetch: pass `session.fetch` as their fetch
import type { DeviceCollector, DeviceSignals } from "./device";
import { createDeviceCollector } from "./device";
import { OPERATIONS } from "./operations";
import { MgplGraphQLError, type GraphQLErrorItem } from "./transport";
import type { LoginResult, User } from "./types";

/** What the manager keeps. Only the access token is required (e.g. a token from elsewhere). */
export interface StoredSession {
  accessToken: string;
  accessExpiresAt?: string | null;
  refreshToken?: string | null;
  refreshExpiresAt?: string | null;
  user?: User | null;
}

/**
 * Where the tokens live. Memory (default) is the safest in a browser; localStorage survives reloads
 * and syncs tabs but is readable by any script on the page (XSS). Your choice; implement your own for
 * React Native (SecureStore / Keychain), Electron, cookies via your server, …
 */
export interface SessionStorage {
  get(): StoredSession | null;
  set(value: StoredSession | null): void;
  /** Changes made elsewhere (another tab). Optional. */
  subscribe?(listener: (value: StoredSession | null) => void): () => void;
}

export function memorySessionStorage(initial: StoredSession | null = null): SessionStorage {
  let value = initial;
  return { get: () => value, set: (v) => void (value = v) };
}

/** localStorage (default) or sessionStorage, synced across tabs with the `storage` event. */
export function webSessionStorage(o: { key?: string; storage?: Storage } = {}): SessionStorage {
  const key = o.key ?? "mgpl.session";
  const storage = o.storage ?? (globalThis as { localStorage?: Storage }).localStorage;
  if (!storage) return memorySessionStorage();
  const read = (raw: string | null): StoredSession | null => {
    try {
      const v = raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as StoredSession) : null;
      return v && typeof v.accessToken === "string" ? v : null;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  };
  return {
    get: () => read(storage.getItem(key)),
    set: (v) => (v ? storage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(v)) : storage.removeItem(key)),
    subscribe(listener) {
      const w = globalThis as { addEventListener?: Window["addEventListener"]; removeEventListener?: Window["removeEventListener"] };
      if (!w.addEventListener) return () => {};
      const on = (e: StorageEvent) => e.key === key && listener(read(e.newValue));
      w.addEventListener("storage", on);
      return () => w.removeEventListener?.("storage", on);
    },
  };
}

export type SessionStatus = "signed_in" | "signed_out";
/** Why the session ended: the user logged out, the refresh token was refused, or it expired. */
export type SignOutReason = "logout" | "refresh_failed" | "expired";

/** An immutable snapshot (same object until something changes), safe for useSyncExternalStore. */
export interface SessionSnapshot {
  status: SessionStatus;
  user: User | null;
  accessExpiresAt: string | null;
  refreshExpiresAt: string | null;
}

export interface SessionManagerOptions {
  /** The API's GraphQL endpoint (used for refreshSession). Default "/graphql". */
  url?: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  /** Default: memory. */
  storage?: SessionStorage;
  /** Device signals sent with login and refresh. Default: createDeviceCollector(). false: send none. */
  device?: DeviceCollector | false;
  /** Refresh this long before the access token expires. Default 30 s. */
  refreshMarginMs?: number;
  /** Extra headers on the refresh request. */
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  onSignedOut?: (reason: SignOutReason) => void;
}

export interface SessionManager {
  getSnapshot(): SessionSnapshot;
  /** Calls `listener` with each new snapshot; returns the unsubscribe function. */
  subscribe(listener: (snapshot: SessionSnapshot) => void): () => void;
  /** Svelte-style readable store: calls `run` at once and on every change. */
  readonly store: { subscribe(run: (snapshot: SessionSnapshot) => void): () => void };
  /** A valid access token, refreshed first when it is about to expire; null when signed out. */
  accessToken(): Promise<string | null>;
  /** Trades the refresh token for a new pair (one request at a time across calls and tabs). True when it worked. */
  refresh(): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Keeps the tokens from login / refreshSession. */
  signIn(result: LoginResult | StoredSession): void;
  /** Forgets the tokens locally (call the API's logout first to end the session on the server). */
  signOut(reason?: SignOutReason): void;
  /** The current tokens (e.g. the refresh token for logout). */
  current(): StoredSession | null;
  /** Device signals for login (undefined when disabled). */
  device(): Promise<DeviceSignals | undefined>;
  /** `{ authorization: "Bearer …" }` (refreshed first when needed), or {}: for clients that take headers. */
  headers(): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
  /**
   * A fetch that adds the access token and, on UNAUTHENTICATED, refreshes once and retries. Give it
   * to Apollo (HttpLink fetch), urql (fetch), graphql-request, ky, axios adapters, or call it directly.
   */
  fetch: typeof fetch;
}

const REFRESH = OPERATIONS.refreshSession.document;
const LOCK = "mgpl-session-refresh";

const toStored = (r: LoginResult | StoredSession): StoredSession =>
  "refreshToken" in r && "accessExpiresAt" in r
    ? { accessToken: r.accessToken, accessExpiresAt: r.accessExpiresAt ?? null, refreshToken: r.refreshToken ?? null, refreshExpiresAt: r.refreshExpiresAt ?? null, user: r.user ?? null }
    : (r as StoredSession);

async function isUnauthenticated(res: Response): Promise<boolean> {
  if (res.status === 401) return true;
  if (!(res.headers.get("content-type") ?? "").includes("json")) return false;
  try {
    const body = (await res.clone().json()) as { errors?: GraphQLErrorItem[] };
    return !!body?.errors?.some((e) => e.extensions?.code === "UNAUTHENTICATED");
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export function createSessionManager(o: SessionManagerOptions = {}): SessionManager {
  const url = o.url ?? "/graphql";
  const doFetch = o.fetch ?? ((...a: Parameters<typeof fetch>) => fetch(...a));
  const storage = o.storage ?? memorySessionStorage();
  const device = o.device === false ? null : (o.device ?? createDeviceCollector());
  const margin = o.refreshMarginMs ?? 30_000;
  const listeners = new Set<(s: SessionSnapshot) => void>();
  let snapshot: SessionSnapshot = snap(storage.get());
  let inflight: Promise<boolean> | undefined;

  function snap(v: StoredSession | null): SessionSnapshot {
    return { status: v ? "signed_in" : "signed_out", user: v?.user ?? null, accessExpiresAt: v?.accessExpiresAt ?? null, refreshExpiresAt: v?.refreshExpiresAt ?? null };
  }
  function emit(v: StoredSession | null) {
    const next = snap(v);
    if (next.status === snapshot.status && next.user === snapshot.user && next.accessExpiresAt === snapshot.accessExpiresAt && next.refreshExpiresAt === snapshot.refreshExpiresAt) return;
    snapshot = next;
    for (const l of [...listeners]) l(snapshot);
  }
  function save(v: StoredSession | null) {
    storage.set(v);
    emit(v);
  }
  // another tab signed in, refreshed or signed out
  storage.subscribe?.((v) => emit(v));

  const expiresSoon = (v: StoredSession) => !!v.accessExpiresAt && Date.parse(v.accessExpiresAt) - margin <= Date.now();
  const refreshDead = (v: StoredSession) => !v.refreshToken || (!!v.refreshExpiresAt && Date.parse(v.refreshExpiresAt) <= Date.now());

  function signOut(reason: SignOutReason = "logout") {
    const had = !!storage.get();
    save(null);
    if (had) o.onSignedOut?.(reason);
  }

  async function runRefresh(): Promise<boolean> {
    const before = storage.get();
    if (!before?.refreshToken) return false;
    const work = async (): Promise<boolean> => {
      // another tab may have refreshed while we waited for the lock: use its tokens
      const cur = storage.get();
      if (!cur) return false;
      if (cur.refreshToken !== before.refreshToken && !expiresSoon(cur)) {
        emit(cur);
        return true;
      }
      if (refreshDead(cur)) {
        signOut("expired");
        return false;
      }
      let res: Response;
      try {
        res = await doFetch(url, {
          method: "POST",
          headers: { "content-type": "application/json", accept: "application/graphql-response+json, application/json", ...o.headers },
          body: JSON.stringify({ query: REFRESH, variables: { refreshToken: cur.refreshToken, device: device ? await device.get().catch(() => undefined) : undefined } }),
        });
      } catch (e) {
        throw new MgplGraphQLError((e as Error).message || "Network error", [], 0); // offline: keep the session
      }
      const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as { data?: { refreshSession?: LoginResult } | null; errors?: GraphQLErrorItem[] } | null;
      const pair = body?.data?.refreshSession;
      if (pair) {
        save(toStored(pair));
        return true;
      }
      const code = body?.errors?.[0]?.extensions?.code;
      if (code === "INVALID_TOKEN" || code === "UNAUTHENTICATED") {
        signOut("refresh_failed");
        return false;
      }
      throw new MgplGraphQLError(body?.errors?.map((e) => e.message).join("; ") || `${res.status} ${res.statusText}`.trim(), body?.errors ?? [], res.status);
    };
    // one refresh across tabs (Web Locks), where the platform has them
    const locks = (globalThis as { navigator?: { locks?: { request(name: string, cb: () => Promise<boolean>): Promise<boolean> } } }).navigator?.locks;
    return locks ? locks.request(LOCK, work) : work();
  }

  const manager: SessionManager = {
    getSnapshot: () => snapshot,
    subscribe(listener) {
      listeners.add(listener);
      return () => void listeners.delete(listener);
    },
    store: {
      subscribe(run) {
        run(snapshot);
        return manager.subscribe(run);
      },
    },
    async accessToken() {
      const v = storage.get();
      if (!v) return null;
      if (expiresSoon(v) && v.refreshToken) {
        await manager.refresh();
        return storage.get()?.accessToken ?? null;
      }
      return v.accessToken;
    },
    refresh() {
      return (inflight ??= runRefresh().finally(() => (inflight = undefined)));
    },
    signIn(result) {
      save(toStored(result));
    },
    signOut,
    current: () => storage.get(),
    async device() {
      return device ? device.get().catch(() => undefined) : undefined;
    },
    async headers(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
      const t = await manager.accessToken();
      return t ? { authorization: `Bearer ${t}` } : {};
    },
    async fetch(input, init) {
      const send = async () => {
        const headers = new Headers(init?.headers);
        const t = await manager.accessToken();
        if (t) headers.set("authorization", `Bearer ${t}`);
        return doFetch(input, { ...init, headers });
      };
      const res = await send();
      if (storage.get()?.refreshToken && (await isUnauthenticated(res)) && (await manager.refresh())) return send();
      return res;
    },
  };
  return manager;
}
```

## File: src/graphql/transport.ts

```ts
// The GraphQL transport: one POST per operation to the backend's single endpoint (mgpl-diagnostics/api).
import type { SessionManager } from "./session";

export interface GraphQLClientOptions {
  /** The endpoint: "/graphql" (same origin) or "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql". */
  url?: string;
  /** Custom fetch (tests, SSR, retry wrappers). */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  /**
   * The session manager (tokens, refresh, device signals). The GraphQL client creates one in memory
   * when you don't pass it; pass your own for persistence, cross-tab sync or sharing with other libraries.
   */
  session?: SessionManager;
  /** Starting access token (without a session manager, or to seed the default one). */
  token?: string | null;
  /** Called whenever the access token changes (login, refresh, logout). */
  onToken?: (token: string | null) => void;
  /** Extra headers on every request. */
  headers?: HeadersInit | (() => HeadersInit | Promise<HeadersInit>);
  /** e.g. "include" when the API sits behind a cookie-forwarding proxy. */
  credentials?: RequestCredentials;
}

/** One GraphQL error as the server sends it. `code` is the stable part (see the API's docs/05-errors.md). */
export interface GraphQLErrorItem {
  message: string;
  path?: (string | number)[];
  extensions?: { code?: string; [key: string]: unknown };
}

/**
 * Thrown when a response carries errors (or the HTTP request fails). `code` is the first error's
 * code: UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, BAD_USER_INPUT, PERIOD_LOCKED, … .
 */
export class MgplGraphQLError extends Error {
  readonly code: string;
  constructor(
    message: string,
    readonly errors: GraphQLErrorItem[],
    readonly status: number,
    /** Whatever data came back next to the errors. */
    readonly data?: unknown,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "MgplGraphQLError";
    this.code = errors[0]?.extensions?.code ?? (status >= 500 ? "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR" : "NETWORK_ERROR");
  }
}

export type Variables = Record<string, unknown>;

export function createTransport(opts: GraphQLClientOptions = {}) {
  const url = opts.url ?? "/graphql";
  const doFetch = opts.fetch ?? ((...a: Parameters<typeof fetch>) => fetch(...a));
  const session = opts.session;
  let token: string | null = opts.token ?? null;

  async function once<T>(query: string, variables: Variables | undefined, init: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<T> {
      const headers = new Headers(typeof opts.headers === "function" ? await opts.headers() : opts.headers);
      headers.set("content-type", "application/json");
      headers.set("accept", "application/graphql-response+json, application/json");
      const bearer = session ? await session.accessToken() : token;
      if (bearer) headers.set("authorization", `Bearer ${bearer}`);
      let res: Response;
      try {
        res = await doFetch(url, { method: "POST", headers, credentials: opts.credentials, body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }), signal: init.signal });
      } catch (e) {
        throw new MgplGraphQLError((e as Error).message || "Network error", [], 0);
      }
      let body: { data?: T | null; errors?: GraphQLErrorItem[] } | undefined;
      try {
        body = (await res.json()) as typeof body;
      } catch {
        throw new MgplGraphQLError(`${res.status} ${res.statusText}`.trim(), [], res.status);
      }
      if (body?.errors?.length) throw new MgplGraphQLError(body.errors.map((e) => e.message).join("; "), body.errors, res.status, body.data);
      if (!res.ok || body?.data == null) throw new MgplGraphQLError(`${res.status} ${res.statusText}`.trim(), [], res.status);
      return body.data;
  }

  return {
    url,
    session,
    getToken: () => (session ? (session.current()?.accessToken ?? null) : token),
    /** Sets (or clears) the access token by hand. With a session manager, prefer session.signIn. */
    setToken(next: string | null) {
      if (session) {
        if (next) session.signIn({ ...session.current(), accessToken: next });
        else session.signOut("logout");
      } else {
        token = next;
        opts.onToken?.(next);
      }
    },
    /**
     * Runs any operation. Throws MgplGraphQLError on errors; returns `data` otherwise. With a session,
     * an UNAUTHENTICATED answer triggers one refresh and one retry.
     */
    async request<T = unknown>(query: string, variables?: Variables, init: { signal?: AbortSignal } = {}): Promise<T> {
      try {
        return await once<T>(query, variables, init);
      } catch (e) {
        if (session && e instanceof MgplGraphQLError && e.code === "UNAUTHENTICATED" && session.current()?.refreshToken && (await session.refresh())) {
          return once<T>(query, variables, init);
        }
        throw e;
      }
    },
  };
}

export type Transport = ReturnType<typeof createTransport>;
```

// What the client's operations return: the API's GraphQL types (mgpl-diagnostics/api, schema.graphql)

// ISO strings; Day values are "YYYY-MM-DD" (IST). The API's contract test validates every operation.

## File: src/index.ts

```ts
// @mgpl-diagnostics/client — headless browser SDK for the MGPL Diagnostics backend
// (report-kit / invoice-kit API). Zero dependencies. No UI, no CSS: build any UI/UX on top of it.
import type {
  InvoiceRequest,
  InvoiceSampleInfo,
  InvoiceTotals,
  InvoiceInput,
  PriceEntry,
  ReportRequest,
  SampleInfo,
  TemplateCatalog,
} from "./types";

export * from "./types";

// The GraphQL SDK for mgpl-diagnostics/api (one endpoint for everything). Its types are under `Gql`
// here, or flat in "@mgpl-diagnostics/client/graphql".
export {
  createMgplGraphQLClient,
  documentBlob,
  csvBlob,
  createTransport,
  MgplGraphQLError,
  OPERATIONS,
  FRAGMENTS,
  withFragments,
  createSessionManager,
  memorySessionStorage,
  webSessionStorage,
  createDeviceCollector,
  clearOnSignOut,
  mgplFetcher,
  mgplKey,
  mgplMutation,
  mgplQuery,
  runOperation,
} from "./graphql/index";
export type {
  MgplGraphQLClient, MgplGraphQLClientOptions, GraphQLClientOptions, GraphQLErrorItem, Operation, OperationName,
  SessionManager, SessionManagerOptions, SessionSnapshot, SessionStatus, SessionStorage, SignOutReason, StoredSession,
  DeviceCollector, DeviceOptions, DeviceSignals, DeviceStore, RequestClient,
} from "./graphql/index";
export type * as Gql from "./graphql/types";

/** Default mount point of the backend */
export const DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "/api/mgpl";

/** Backend routes, relative to the base URL */
export const ROUTES = {
  health: "/health",
  templates: "/templates",
  samples: "/samples",
  report: "/report",
  letterhead: "/letterhead",
  assets: "/assets",
  invoice: "/invoice",
  priceList: "/price-list",
  invoiceSamples: "/invoice-samples",
} as const;

export interface ClientOptions {
  /** Backend URL: "/api/mgpl" (same origin) or "https://api.example.com/api/mgpl" */
  baseUrl?: string;
  /** Custom fetch (tests, SSR, auth/retry wrappers) */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  /** Headers on every request, e.g. () => ({ Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }) */
  headers?: HeadersInit | (() => HeadersInit | Promise<HeadersInit>);
  /** e.g. "include" for cookie auth across origins */
  credentials?: RequestCredentials;
}

/** Any non-2xx response. `message` is the server's error text, `status` the HTTP status. */
export class MgplApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    public status: number,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "MgplApiError";
  }
}

type Query = Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>;

export function createMgplClient(opts: ClientOptions = {}) {
  const baseUrl = (opts.baseUrl ?? DEFAULT_BASE_URL).replace(/\/$/, "");
  const doFetch = opts.fetch ?? ((...a: Parameters<typeof fetch>) => fetch(...a));

  const url = (path: string, query?: Query) => {
    const qs = query
      ? Object.entries(query)
          .filter(([, v]) => v !== undefined && v !== false)
          .map(([k, v]) => `${encodeURIComponent(k)}=${encodeURIComponent(String(v))}`)
          .join("&")
      : "";
    return `${baseUrl}${path}${qs ? `?${qs}` : ""}`;
  };

  async function call(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}, query?: Query): Promise<Response> {
    const headers = new Headers(typeof opts.headers === "function" ? await opts.headers() : opts.headers);
    new Headers(init.headers).forEach((v, k) => headers.set(k, v));
    const res = await doFetch(url(path, query), { ...init, headers, credentials: opts.credentials });
    if (!res.ok) {
      let msg = `${res.status} ${res.statusText}`.trim();
      try {
        const body = (await res.json()) as { error?: string };
        if (body.error) msg = body.error;
      } catch {
        /* not JSON */
      }
      throw new MgplApiError(msg, res.status);
    }
    return res;
  }
  const post = (path: string, body: unknown) =>
    call(path, { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(body) });

  return {
    baseUrl,
    /** URL of a route (for <a href>, <iframe src>, window.open) */
    url,
    health: (): Promise<{ ok: boolean }> => call(ROUTES.health).then((r) => r.json()),

    reports: {
      /** Every test template with its result fields (build entry forms from this) + profiles */
      templates: (): Promise<TemplateCatalog> => call(ROUTES.templates).then((r) => r.json()),
      /** Demo reports (only when the server enables samples) */
      samples: (): Promise<SampleInfo[]> => call(ROUTES.samples).then((r) => r.json()),
      /** A4 PDF */
      pdf: (req: ReportRequest): Promise<Blob> => post(ROUTES.report, { ...req, format: "pdf" }).then((r) => r.blob()),
      /** HTML document (its fonts/images load from the backend) — show it in <HtmlFrame> or an iframe */
      html: (req: ReportRequest): Promise<string> => post(ROUTES.report, { ...req, format: "html" }).then((r) => r.text()),
      letterheadPdf: (): Promise<Blob> => call(ROUTES.letterhead, {}, { format: "pdf" }).then((r) => r.blob()),
      letterheadHtml: (): Promise<string> => call(ROUTES.letterhead, {}, { format: "html" }).then((r) => r.text()),
      /** Direct link to the letterhead PDF */
      letterheadUrl: (download = false) => url(ROUTES.letterhead, { format: "pdf", download: download ? 1 : undefined }),
    },

    invoices: {
      /** Price list (codes usable as invoice items) */
      priceList: (): Promise<PriceEntry[]> => call(ROUTES.priceList).then((r) => r.json()),
      samples: (): Promise<InvoiceSampleInfo[]> => call(ROUTES.invoiceSamples).then((r) => r.json()),
      /** Server-side calculation: totals, GST, round-off, status, amount in words */
      totals: (invoice: InvoiceInput): Promise<InvoiceTotals> => post(ROUTES.invoice, { invoice, format: "json" }).then((r) => r.json()),
      pdf: (req: InvoiceRequest): Promise<Blob> => post(ROUTES.invoice, { ...req, format: "pdf" }).then((r) => r.blob()),
      html: (req: InvoiceRequest): Promise<string> => post(ROUTES.invoice, { ...req, format: "html" }).then((r) => r.text()),
    },
  };
}

export type MgplClient = ReturnType<typeof createMgplClient>;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ browser utils */

/** Save a Blob as a file. */
export function downloadBlob(blob: Blob, fileName: string): void {
  const href = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = href;
  a.download = fileName;
  document.body.appendChild(a);
  a.click();
  a.remove();
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(href), 60_000);
}

/** Open a Blob (e.g. a PDF) in a new tab. */
export function openBlob(blob: Blob): void {
  const href = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  window.open(href, "_blank", "noopener");
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(href), 60_000);
}

/** Print a PDF Blob through a hidden iframe. */
export function printBlob(blob: Blob): void {
  const href = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const frame = document.createElement("iframe");
  frame.style.cssText = "position:fixed;right:0;bottom:0;width:0;height:0;border:0";
  frame.src = href;
  frame.onload = () => {
    frame.contentWindow?.focus();
    frame.contentWindow?.print();
    setTimeout(() => {
      frame.remove();
      URL.revokeObjectURL(href);
    }, 60_000);
  };
  document.body.appendChild(frame);
}
```
